headers.//: The HTML shell and the runtime JSON must never be served from an edge cache without asking the origin first. Vercel was holding `/` at the edge for the better part of an hour (x-vercel-cache: HIT, age: 3409) and a query string does not change the cache key for a static file, so a stale entry survives both a hard refresh and a cache-buster. Because the shell names the content-hashed bundle, one stale copy of it serves an entire old app off assets that are still around. max-age=0 only governs the browser; s-maxage=0 is what tells the CDN to revalidate. /assets/* is deliberately untouched — it is content-addressed, so it is safe to cache forever and that is where the caching actually pays.
